forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Derbyshire Dales faces £4.2m budget gap by 2029/30 with no savings plan yet in place
news_drafts.lead: Derbyshire Dales District Council will need to find nearly £1m in savings in 2027/28 to balance its budget, with the gap widening sharply to over £4m by 2029/30, according to budget monitoring papers presented to council this month. The authority has not yet identified where those savings will come from. Meanwhile, usable capital reserves for new schemes are forecast to fall to just £331,000 by 2031, and the council says future borrowing is unlikely to be affordable given its medium-term financial position. The council is meeting this year's budget partly through one-off income — £281,000 from investment returns and £200,000 from planning fees on a single application — and by drawing down general reserves from £27.3m to £14.6m by March 2027. The council's own risk register rates financial resilience as high risk, pending delivery of required savings and clarity on local government reorganisation costs.

findings.headline: End of waste contract: Waste Options Appraisal and soft market engagement are ongoing, with a report to Council in January 2027
findings.detail: The council is gathering service, operational and financial data for the Waste Options Appraisal and has run soft market engagement on interest in a future waste and recycling contract. The paper describes this work as an evidence base for informed decisions on future service delivery.
findings.matters: A waste contract ending and being retendered or delivered in-house is a large recurring cost decision, and other councils facing similar retender decisions would compare the options and timing.
findings.quote: A report will go to Council in January 2027 with options and recommendations.

findings.headline: Leisure contract options appraisal is considering a 5 year extension with Freedom Leisure, with recommendations to Council in January
findings.detail: Officers are testing the feasibility of options other than the current arrangement, including a five-year extension with Freedom Leisure. A report has already gone to the Performance and Achievement committee, with a further report to Council in January with options and recommendations.
findings.matters: A decision on a leisure management contract, whether to extend or retender, carries a long-term cost and liability that finance officers and lenders would want to see once options are set out.
findings.figures: Proposed extension: 5 year; Council report: January 2027
findings.quote: Officers are exploring feasibility of other options including 5 year extension with Freedom Leisure.

findings.headline: Ashbourne Reborn Levelling Up Fund: final Link Community Hub works moved to end Q3 or early Q4 2026/27
findings.detail: The project was marked Complete in Q1 because the grant-funded elements were done. In Q2 it moved to On Track with Concerns, as the final Church-led and funded works at the Link Community Hub were delayed by on-site issues. A final report is due later in 2026/27.
findings.matters: A capital grant programme whose completion was reported early and then slipped is the kind of delivery change a finance director would track against grant conditions and end dates.
findings.figures: Status: Complete (Q1) to On Track with Concerns (Q2); completion now end Q3 / early Q4 2026/27
findings.quote: the final Church led / funded works at the Link Community Hub were delayed due to on-site issues and now to be completed end Q3 / early Q4.

findings.headline: Second homes fell by 98, from 905 to 807 properties, in the quarter, the third successive quarterly reduction
findings.detail: The paper attributes the reduction to properties being sold or privately rented, with some occupied as principal homes and a small number converted to holiday accommodation. Holiday lets fell by 10 in the same quarter.
findings.matters: Council tax income from second homes depends on the premium and on the stock of second homes, so a finance officer at another council would want to see whether a similar trend is happening locally.
findings.figures: Second homes 905 to 807 properties (down 98); holiday lets down 10 in the quarter
findings.quote: The number of second homes has reduced for the 3rd successive quarter by 98 from 905 to 807 properties.

findings.headline: Council tax in-year collection was 61.30% at Q2 2026/27 against a 61% Q2 target, reported as on track
findings.detail: The paper gives Q1 outturn of 33.50% against a 33% Q1 target and Q2 outturn of 61.30% against a 61% Q2 target, with both quarters marked On track.
findings.matters: Council tax collection is a core income line, and a finance director would compare the in-year profile with peers' collection performance.
findings.figures: Q1 outturn 33.50% (Q1 target 33%); Q2 outturn 61.30% (Q2 target 61%); year-end target 98.4%
